items.title: Function app: sub-scoped hardcoded 'JIT Requester' check
items.description: Hardcode role name 'JIT Requester' in the app; remove JIT_REQUESTER_ROLE_NAME env usage. Change Test-CallerHasJitRequesterRole (JITHelpers.psm1:~315) to derive the subscription from the request body target subscriptionId instead of the site resource ID, resolve the role by name within the TARGET subscription, and check the caller's assignment at target-sub scope. Ensure the 'JIT Requester' role definition exists in each target subscription (Deploy.ps1/Grant-JITPermissions.ps1 create it per target sub). Keep 'JIT-AzAccess Manager' MI role untouched. Existing add-IP-to-whitelist + schedule-removal flow unchanged.

comments.author: developer
comments.text: Implemented. Two read endpoints had no request-body target sub, so a judgment call was made: Revoke-JITAccess checks against the rule's own subscription (row.SubscriptionId); Get-JITRules checks against the app's derived HOST subscription (it only returns the caller's own rules). Consequence: a user needs 'JIT Requester' in the host subscription to LIST rules, and in each target subscription to request/revoke there. Deploy Step 4 keeps the host sub in the role's assignableScopes so it isn't orphaned. NEEDS ARCHITECT/USER CONFIRMATION - listing one's own rules requiring a host-sub role may be undesirable.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: DECISION (user, 2026-07-16): Get-JITRules should have NO role check - any authenticated caller lists only their own rules. Follow-up change: remove the Test-CallerHasJitRequesterRole gate from Get-JITRules/run.ps1 (keep JWT/caller-identity validation for filtering), and drop the host subscription from the role's assignableScopes (revert Deploy.ps1 Step 4 host-sub merge). Requester role now lives ONLY in target subscriptions. Revoke stays checked against the rule's own subscription.

items.title: Fix stale mocks in Remove-ExpiredRules.Tests.ps1 (19 failing tests)
items.description: CORRECTED ROOT CAUSE (verified 2026-07-21): the 19 failing Remove-ExpiredRules.Tests.ps1 tests are NOT a Pester 3.4/PS7 incompatibility. Plain Pester 3.4 Mock/Assert-MockCalled works fine under PS7 (the 6 new postgres tests pass). The real cause: the stale BeforeEach mocks commands that no longer exist in the code (Get-JITCloudTable, Get-AzTableRow, Remove-AzTableRow) - Pester 3 cannot mock a nonexistent command, so every test in those Describes fails at setup with 'Could not find Command Get-JITCloudTable'. FIX: repoint those mocks to the current JITHelpers functions Get-JITTableName/Get-JITTableRows/Remove-JITTableRow (as the new postgres Describe already does) - NOT a Pester upgrade. SEPARATE/UNVERIFIED: the 2 JITHelpers.Tests.ps1 'Should Throw' failures were not re-diagnosed and may be a distinct issue. No CI runs these tests (publish-plugin.yml only builds the C# plugin).

comments.author: developer
comments.text: Additional finding (2026-07-21): Remove-ExpiredRules.Tests.ps1 mocks are also STALE vs implementation - they mock Get-AzTableRow/Remove-AzTableRow/Get-JITCloudTable, but current run.ps1 uses Get-JITTableRows/Remove-JITTableRow via Invoke-TableRest (not Az.Table). So the dispatch/retry assertions there never hit the real flow. The Pester-v5 upgrade should ALSO rewrite these mocks to the current JITHelpers functions.

items.title: PowerShell script: configure Azure PIM (permanent eligibility) for JIT-Requester across subscriptions
items.description: New src/scripts script. Params: -Subscriptions (list of sub IDs), -ActiveAssignment (Entra group display name -> permanent ACTIVE assignment), -EligibleAssignment (Entra group display name -> permanent ELIGIBLE assignment), -RoleName (default 'JIT-Requester'). Per subscription: resolve role def + group object IDs, relax the role management policy to ALLOW permanent eligibility (and permanent active), then create permanent (NoExpiration) eligible + active PIM assignments. PIM for Azure resources (ARM roleEligibilityScheduleRequests / roleAssignmentScheduleRequests). Idempotent, -WhatIf, per-sub summary. Requires PIM P2 licensing.

comments.author: developer
comments.text: Implemented as src/scripts/Set-JITPim.ps1 (Az.Accounts+Az.Resources; PIM for Azure resources). Verified cmdlet shapes vs MS Learn (azps-16.1.0). Policy relaxation: mutate EffectiveRule entries Expiration_Admin_Eligibility + Expiration_Admin_Assignment IsExpirationRequired=false. Permanent = -ExpirationType NoExpiration + -RequestType AdminAssign on New-AzRoleEligibilityScheduleRequest / New-AzRoleAssignmentScheduleRequest. Idempotent via Get-AzRoleEligibilitySchedule/Get-AzRoleAssignmentSchedule + conflict-catch; 3x15s retry for policy propagation. Syntax PARSE OK. LIVE EXECUTION NOT PERFORMED (no Az.Resources locally; needs P2 + Azure). First-run caveat: policy property assumed $policy.EffectiveRule - if the installed module differs the relaxation step errors clearly per-sub.

items.title: Enrich all JIT error messages with tenantId, subscription, and caller UPN
items.description: Function app: extend Write-JITAuditEvent (JITHelpers.psm1:508-546) with a tenantId field; thread $claims.tid; add tenantId/UPN/subscription to HTTP error bodies (centralize the 3 per-endpoint Write-JsonResponse copies); add the MISSING audit event on the Revoke role-denial (Revoke-JITAccess/run.ps1:104-107). Server already has UPN as $claims.upn. Plugin: add tenantId+subscription+resource to error toast/log Details (in scope at grant/revoke sites GrantFromTargetAsync ~1126, ConfirmRevokeAsync ~1205); put context in Details not the visible Message per INotifier guidance. OPEN DECISION: caller UPN is NOT available in the plugin (host exposes only TenantId+DisplayName; DisplayName is friendly name, not UPN). Options: server includes UPN in error bodies (covers 403 + server errors) and/or plugin fetches Graph GET /me per tenant (cached) for client-side-only errors. Note: expiry/timer path has no live token, so tenantId there needs persisting on the table row at grant time.

items.title: Plugin: retry-with-backoff on 403 role-denied grant (NOT token refresh)
items.description: User asked to 'refresh token and retry' on the 403 'caller does not hold JIT-Requester'. FINDING: token refresh is (a) IMPOSSIBLE via Contracts 1.3.0 - IPluginHttpClient.SendAsync has no forceRefresh, IPluginContext has no cache-invalidation, host overwrites auth header with a cached token; and (b) INEFFECTIVE anyway - server checks RBAC by the caller's stable oid via ARM at call time, not from token claims, so a fresh token changes nothing for a directly-assigned role; the real cause is RBAC propagation delay (~up to 5 min). EFFECTIVE FIX: bounded retry-with-backoff (2-3 attempts, short delay) on JitHttpException.StatusCode==403 inside GrantFromTargetAsync (wraps RequestAccessAsync ~JitAzAccessPlugin.cs:1096-1098); keep total under ~30-45s so the busy row doesn't hang. Branch on status code, not message text (plugin doesn't parse the message). GROUP-assignment edge case genuinely needs a fresh interactive login (host-owned) - only remedy is a re-sign-in guidance toast, or a Contracts enhancement request to host (IPluginContext.InvalidateToken -> existing CredentialFactory.Invalidate). OPEN DECISION: retry+re-sign-in hint vs retry-only vs retry+file host enhancement.

items.title: Reconcile AppName mismatch between Deploy.ps1 and Test-JITAccess.ps1
items.description: Deploy.ps1 uses $AppName='pgjitazaccess' while Test-JITAccess.ps1 defaults $AppName='jitazaccess'. These derive DIFFERENT resource names, so Test-JITAccess may target the wrong (non-existent) function app after a Deploy. Reconcile to a single source of truth.

items.title: Refactor JITTargets.psm1: one file per JIT asset type
items.description: Split Modules/JITTargets/JITTargets.psm1 so each supported asset type (nsg, sqlServer, storageAccount, keyVault, postgresqlFlexibleServer) has its own file under Modules/JITTargets/Targets/. Shared helpers (Wait-JITArmAsyncOperation, Get-HeaderValue, api-version consts, PRIVATE_SERVER_REJECTED sentinel, ARM/status helpers) move to a shared file. JITTargets.psm1 becomes a loader that dot-sources Targets/*.ps1 (shared first) and keeps Export-ModuleMember surface IDENTICAL. Pure move/reorg, no behavior change; consumers (run.ps1 dispatch, profile.ps1) unchanged. Verify module imports + exports identical + test.ps1 baseline unchanged.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Follow-up (user request): move per-type $script constants out of _Shared.ps1 into their own target files (KeyVaultApi->KeyVault.ps1, SqlApi->SqlServer.ps1, NsgApi->Nsg.ps1, StorageMgmtApi->StorageAccount.ps1, PostgresApi + sentinel + LRO bounds->PostgresqlFlexibleServer.ps1). comments.author: developer
comments.text: Follow-up done: moved all 8 per-type $script constants into their target files (NsgApi->Nsg, SqlApi->SqlServer, StorageMgmtApi->StorageAccount, KeyVaultApi->KeyVault, PostgresApi+sentinel+2 LRO bounds->PostgresqlFlexibleServer). Export parity + test baseline (62/41/21) unchanged.

items.title: HOST FIX (AzureTray): dedupe plugin load by Plugin.Id, not AssemblyPath
items.description: Stale/duplicate JIT tray menu after plugin version swap. ROOT CAUSE (host-side): PluginLoader keys load-vs-reload on assembly FILE PATH not Plugin.Id (LoadOrReloadAsync ~L327-329, LoadOneAsync ~L224-227). When the new version's DLL lands at a different path (legacy plugins/<id>.dll -> subfolder plugins/<id>/<id>.dll, or filename change) the host ADDS a second entry instead of unloading the old; both instances' menus show and the orphaned old instance's 90s poll timer roots it (leaked collectible ALC, keeps polling). FIX: before registering a newly loaded plugin, unload any existing _entries item with the same Plugin.Id via UnloadEntryAsync (change reload/idempotency key AssemblyPath->Plugin.Id). Plugin side needs NO change (Dispose/ShutdownAsync already tear down timer+events). Secondary: TrayIcon holds plugin refs in _menuChangeSubscriptions/_badgeSubscriptions cleared on dispatcher after UnloadEntryAsync's GC.Collect, delaying ALC unload even on the correct path. AzureTray repo is READ-ONLY for the agent; patch drafted to c:\tmp for the user to apply.

comments.author: developer
comments.text: Patch drafted + verified with git apply --check: c:\tmp\azuretray-plugin-id-dedupe.patch. Single dedupe-by-Plugin.Id chokepoint in TryLoadAsync (unload existing same-Id entry via UnloadEntryAsync before registering new). Deliberately did NOT change LoadOneAsync idempotency to Id (would block upgrades). Secondary TrayIcon unload-timing fix described only (with primary fix it's just a GC-timing nicety, not a leak). AzureTray repo left untouched (read-only).

items.title: NSG already-whitelisted detection: CIDR/prefixes/service-tag aware
items.description: FEAT-0003 item4: NSG duplicate-detection is best-effort exact-single-IP only (matches an inbound Allow rule whose sourceAddressPrefix == caller IP or /32). It does NOT evaluate CIDR ranges, sourceAddressPrefixes arrays, service tags, or per-port scope, so an IP covered by a broader rule is treated as not-present and a fresh JIT rule is created. Enhancement: make NSG detection range/prefix/service-tag aware if dup-suppression fidelity matters. Documented in code.

items.title: FIXED: Grant-JITPermissions role-definition update KeyError roleName + swallowed az errors
items.description: az role definition UPDATE failed with KeyError:'roleName' because both role update paths (Manager + Requester) sent create-schema payload (Name+Id, no roleName); and az failures were swallowed (no LASTEXITCODE check) so script printed false 'Role updated.'. FIX (verified vs installed az 2.86.0 by disassembling the CLI module): update payloads now send roleName=<display>+name=<GUID>+id + lowercase-first keys (assignableScopes/actions/...); create paths kept in PascalCase; added LASTEXITCODE!=0 throw after all az role definition create/update + role assignment create. Idempotent re-run re-applies Manager actions + adds the 2 missing JIT-Requester scopes (74e22077, d5dc1696). Uncommitted with the rest of the working tree. FOLLOW-UP: Manager $roleActions here is source of truth; adding asset types to plugin AssetTypeCatalog requires syncing Actions here (see TODO drift note).

items.title: Wire target handler Details into the JIT audit rows
items.description: Every JIT target handler returns a Details hashtable, but nothing consumes it: Write-JITAuditEvent is never passed Details from Request-JITAccess/run.ps1, Remove-ExpiredRules/run.ps1, or Revoke-JITAccess/run.ps1. Discovered while implementing FEAT-0004 (App Service slot coverage), which relies on Details.slotFailures / slotEnumerationFailed as the compensating control for a partial revoke. Until Details reaches the audit row, that partial-failure signal is Write-Warning log-only, which undercuts the tradeoff of returning the site outcome when slot enumeration fails. Wire Details into the JITGranted / JITExpired / JITRevoked audit rows.

comments.author: developer
comments.text: Implemented. Two similarly-named functions existed and both prior reports were right about different ones: Write-JITAuditEvent (JITHelpers.psm1:514-552) is the stdout logger and is unchanged; Add-JITAuditRow (:960-1030) is the table writer and is what changed. New internal ConvertTo-JITAuditDetails (:909-958) serializes, bounds, and never throws; Add-JITAuditRow gained an optional [hashtable] Details param stored in a Details column. Deliberately NOT routed through -Extra: -Extra is a flat scalar merge done by the caller, so reusing it would duplicate serialize+truncate+try/catch across all eight call sites, and the never-break-the-operation guarantee is only enforceable in one place. -Extra is untouched and composes alongside Details. JSON depth 6. Truncation cap 8192 chars with 1024-char preview, replaced by a still-valid JSON envelope {_truncated,_originalLength,_preview} rather than a chopped string. Empty or null Details omits the column entirely. Wired 8 call sites, not the 3 named: Request-JITAccess Grant/Extend/AlreadyExternal/SkippedOpen, Revoke-JITAccess Revoke/RemoveFailed, Remove-ExpiredRules Expire/RemoveFailed.

comments.author: testcase
comments.text: 21 new tests in src/functionapp/tests/JITHelpers.Audit.Tests.ps1 (extended, reusing its existing Invoke-TableRest body-capture harness), all passing. Suite 199 -> 220 tests; the 21 failures are byte-identical to baseline, and the 2 JITHelpers.Tests.ps1 failures did not shift despite the psm1 edit. No product bugs. Note: the App Service Details shape survives even at ConvertTo-Json's default depth 2, so it does not by itself prove depth 6 - a separate 5-level-deep test is the real guard. The intentional no-Details omission on the Remove-ExpiredRules outer catch is pinned by AST assertions over the entry points rather than the broken timer harness, so it survives TODO-0006 being fixed later.

items.title: Two failing JITHelpers tests outside TODO-0006's scope
items.description: Baseline suite has 21 failures, but TODO-0006 only covers the 19 in Remove-ExpiredRules.Tests.ps1. Two more live in JITHelpers.Tests.ps1 and are untracked: 'Invoke-JwtValidation > rejects an empty string token (parameter binding rejects it)' and 'Get-AvailableNsgPriority > throws when every priority in the range is occupied'. Both predate FEAT-0004. Note for whoever picks this up: Pester 3.4.0's 'Should Throw' is broken under PowerShell 7 on this machine - a minimal repro of { throw 'boom' } | Should Throw fails - so both of these may be harness artifacts rather than product bugs. AppService.Tests.ps1 works around it with a local Test-Throws try/catch helper; reuse that pattern.

items.title: build.ps1 does not validate the PowerShell function app
items.description: build.ps1 only builds the C# plugin (AzureTray.Plugin.JITAzAccess), so the bulk of this repo - src/functionapp/**/*.ps1 - gets no build-time validation at all. Surfaced during FEAT-0004, where the developer had to hand-run [Parser]::ParseFile over the changed files to get any signal. Add a -Target FunctionApp mode that parse-checks every function app .ps1 and optionally runs PSScriptAnalyzer, so the convention script actually covers the project.

items.title: Stale $removeResult in the Remove-ExpiredRules outer catch
items.description: The timer's outer catch in src/functionapp/Remove-ExpiredRules/run.ps1 (~:146-173) sits inside a foreach over rows, so $removeResult still holds the PREVIOUS iteration's value when the handler throws. Nothing reads it there today, so it is currently harmless - TODO-0017 deliberately omitted -Details from that RemoveFailed audit call for exactly this reason, and the omission is pinned by an AST assertion in JITHelpers.Audit.Tests.ps1. But it is a live trap: the next person to reference $removeResult in that block will silently attribute one resource's state to another. Null the variable at the top of each loop iteration, or scope it so the catch cannot see a stale value.

items.title: Split JITHelpers.psm1 - multi-responsibility module at ~1030 lines
items.description: src/functionapp/Modules/JITHelpers/JITHelpers.psm1 is now roughly 1030 lines and holds JWT validation, RBAC checks, Graph tag lookups, blob locking, table CRUD, audit writers (both the stdout Write-JITAuditEvent and the table Add-JITAuditRow), and caller-IP extraction. Well past the 500-line flag threshold and a genuine multi-responsibility module rather than a formatting issue. Flagged during TODO-0017. Wants a design pass on the split before anyone starts moving functions - the module is imported by all four entry points, so the seams matter.

items.title: Pester 3.4 + PowerShell 7 gotchas for this repo's tests
items.description: Two harness traps confirmed on this machine, both of which cost real debugging time and will hit the next person writing tests here. (1) 'Should Throw' is broken: a minimal repro of { throw 'boom' } | Should Throw fails. Use a local Test-Throws try/catch helper instead - src/functionapp/tests/AppService.Tests.ps1 has one, and JITHelpers.Audit.Tests.ps1 copies it. (2) Mocks declared inside an It are torn down at Describe/Context exit, NOT per-It, so a failure-injection mock (e.g. a throwing ConvertTo-Json) leaks forward into later Its in the same block. Quarantine any such mock in its own Context. Worth folding into CLAUDE.md or a testing README rather than leaving as a tracking item, if there is a natural home for it.

items.title: Guard against the single-added-scope StrictMode crash pattern
items.description: Grant-JITPermissions.ps1's assignable-scope merge used $added = $scopes | Where-Object {...} then $added.Count. Under Set-StrictMode -Version Latest, a single match returns a bare [string] and .Count is a terminating error - so the scope-merge path had never actually worked in the single-added-subscription case, which is the most common one. Fixed in place by wrapping both $added and $addedReq in @(). Worth a sweep of the other scripts in src/scripts/ for the same unguarded pipeline-result-dot-Count pattern, since they all run under StrictMode.
